summary:
Every lunar landing mission starts with one question:

"Is it safe to land here?"   

Landing near the Moon's south pole means working with the Sun barely above the horizon and Earth sometimes dropping out of sight. A crater rim a few kilometres away can decide whether your solar panels get light or whether you can call home. 

That is why we built Ridgeline, a zero-install, all in one, 3D lunar landing site navigator running right in your browser. Pick a candidate site, or drop a pin anywhere, and Ridgeline traces the real horizon around it using NASA terrain data. It then tracks the Sun and Earth across that skyline using JPL's planetary ephemeris. You get countdowns, light and comms timelines, and a 3D view of the terrain. Close to the pole, where small terrain errors matter a lot, we show a window of possible times rather than one exact time.

We checked our math directly against NASA JPL Horizons and SPICE, and published every test result inside the app, including the ones that fail so teams can make fast, trustworthy landing decisions.
details:
Ridgeline is a web-based interactive 3D lunar landing site navigator designed to evaluate sunlight availability and direct-to-Earth communication windows at candidate landing sites on the Moon. Traditionally, checking how crater shadows and launch delays affect lunar missions requires navigating complex, separate NASA tools and raw datasets. Our platform uniquely brings 3D terrain, solar power modeling, communication sightlines, and open physics verification into one instant browser workspace.

How it works:

Ridgeline combines 60-meter NASA LRO LOLA polar elevation maps with NASA JPL planetary ephemeris math to trace the real 360-degree crater horizon around any historic mission site or custom lunar coordinate. It calculates live sunset and Earthset countdowns, renders 30×30 km 3D terrain sightlines, and lets users compare up to four landing sites side by side across changing launch dates, solar panel rules, and Deep Space Network visibility limits with every calculation openly benchmarked against JPL Horizons and SPICE inside the app.

Key Benefits & Impact:

  • Helps CLPS and mission planners rapidly re-evaluate backup sites and power budgets when launch dates slip.
  • Aids lunar researchers in auditing local crater-rim shadows and south pole uncertainty windows without writing custom scripts.
  • Supports educators and students in exploring 56 years of real lunar landings and orbital geometry in 3D.
  • Offers visual, zero-install access to flight-grade NASA ephemeris and topography data on any browser.

Tools & Technologies:

  • React, TypeScript & Vite: front-end web application and interactive mission planner interface
  • Three.js / WebGL & Blender: 3D lunar globe asset creation and 30×30 km local surface mesh visualization
  • Rasterio, Pyproj, NumPy & SciPy: geospatial processing of 60-meter NASA LRO LOLA DEMs, coordinate transformations, and terrain horizon calculations
  • Python, SpiceyPy & Pytest: NAIF SPICE reference validation pipeline, automated unit testing, and 1,000-case accuracy benchmarking against NASA JPL Horizons
  • Matplotlib: validation diagnostics and accuracy verification plots
  • Vercel & GitHub: cloud deployment and version control
  • CapCut & Canva: Project demo video editing and pitch presentation graphics
  • Youtube: Project demo video submission
